messages:
laura: Quick sync — RFC follow-up on 'Auth surface unification'. I sketched a minimal path to converge API keys + service tokens into a single externally-facing token type (short-lived, aud-scoped). Want feedback on migration pain and SDK impact.

mike: TL;dr? wondering if this breaks existing long-lived api keys we hand out to customers.

laura: Good call. Goal is to keep long-lived creds for self-managed/private users but *represent* them via minting short-lived tokens at the edge for runtime requests. So we introduce a minting service that issues v2 tokens.

deepa: That sounds similar to broker idea from last year. Differences?

laura: Yeah similar but narrower: 1) unify headers so callers always send Authorization: Bearer <v2-token>. 2) internal services can still present old api-key in side-channel to mint v2. 3) token contains aud and scope claims instead of opaque project_id header.

jonathan: How do we handle RBAC? aud + scope mapping seems fine, but policy layer needs to support both project-scoped and org-scoped claims during transition.

deepa: We should avoid a big DB migration. Prefer mapping table in authz service: if token has org claim -> map to org-role; project claim -> project-role. We can treat api-key legacy as a principal with fixed mapping.

mike: SDK changes? We need to make client SDKs auto-refresh v2 tokens. Customers using raw curl might be ok if we document mint endpoint.

laura: Proposed delta for SDKs: add AuthClient.mint(token_kind="v2", ttl=300) and automatic header injection when using Redwood API clients. Keep opt-out to preserve explicit header users.

sam-bot: deploybot: posted draft RFC at https://r.example.com/rfc/auth-unify (ops:review) :white_check_mark:

jonathan: One risk: audit trails. Right now api-keys map directly to owner. If we mint ephemeral tokens, audit must persist original api-key id -> minted token id mapping. We should log both.

deepa: +1. Also add revocation path: revoke original api-key -> invalidate outstanding v2 tokens (via token blacklist / issuance epoch).

mike: Latency concern: adding mint step on every call will blow P99. We should recommend client-side caching of v2 token for the TTL and server-side caching in the edge. TTL maybe 5m by default.

laura: Agreed. Proposal: default TTL 5m, SDK caches and refreshes proactively at 80% expiry. Edge caches per (principal, scope) to avoid mint storm.

jonathan: Back-compat plan: 1) Lighthouse rollout where API accepts both Authorization: Bearer v1-opaque and v2; 2) Logging + monitoring for mismatches; 3) Deprecation window 6 months for hosted customers, longer for enterprise with plan.

deepa: Can we reuse existing introspection endpoint for v2? Keep same endpoint but return richer claims JSON.

laura: Yes — extend introspect to return aud, scopes[], issued_by, parent_key_id. Minimal breaking change.

mike: Need a small RFC appendix on migration scripts: map legacy key ids -> parent_key_id in audit logs, and create revocation cron.

laura: I'll update the draft with: minting flow diagram, SDK snippets, TTL defaults, revocation model, and the rollout timeline. Action items: laura update RFC, deepa draft introspect changes, jonathan add audit schema, mike draft SDK PR. Ping me in-thread when ready. :rocket:
